topLevel: the probe project is the probe, the instrument and four small files, at the paths the probe preloads, with the repository's instrument and the hash of every file
the project's texts: a minimal project.godot on civ-lite's renderer, an entry class that extends the probe by name, an empty scene, and override.cfg naming both
a directory that is not new is refused, an absent or empty one is made, and a failed import is refused with its log
the arguments of each entry are pure: script keeps today's, main-loop and release have no --script, and a report that is not absolute is refused

the main-loop entry runs the editor over the probe project with no --script, and the release entry runs the exported .app from the check's own directory; both leave the report in the check's directory
the script entry is what it was: the report is a name under the checkout's build directory and is copied to the check's directory
the three entries judge the same way: the oracle, the log, the probe's own checks, the display of a window and the instrument's hash
the timeout of the process is the check's to set, and an entry that lacks what it runs is refused before anything starts
a good manifest has no problem, and each way of being wrong is named
the three manifests are read from <directory>/<arm>, with their paths resolved to absolute ones
prepare() registers what the manifests say, with the seed, the game's hashes and the instrument from the Debug launcher's sources
prepare() refuses, naming the arm and the file, when a manifest is missing, is wrong or does not match its file, and nothing runs
launch() runs the executable of the arm with the scenario's arguments, with no -s and an absolute --out, in a directory outside the .app and the exports
a real process of the fake .app: the report is read, the launch has the interface's shape, and the working directory is the launcher's own
a process that exits with an error, writes no report or writes a report of its own is passed on as it came
a process killed while it wrote its report leaves a file that is not JSON: no report, the file is kept, the log says where, and cleanup() leaves it
a file that changed between prepare() and launch() makes launch() throw, and the process is not started
a process that outlives the launcher's timeout is killed and is reported as timed out, and only then
cleanup() removes the launcher's own directory and nothing of the exports
the campaign reads and validates the exports, then refuses because the instrument's self-check cannot run in a template, before anything is launched or written
the command line: --build release needs --exports, which a Debug rehearsal does not take, and the campaign refuses with the self-check's reason and runs nothing
the probe's export is read like an arm's when the directory has it, and is none when it does not
prepare() with the probe's export makes the launcher's self-check the exported probe, and without it the self-check stays unsupported
prepare() refuses a probe export that is not the registered one, or that is not from the arms' template, and the self-check stays unsupported
the self-check through the release entry runs the probe's .app with --report, in a directory outside the .app and the exports, and judges it as the other entries do
the campaign with the probe's export runs the self-check through the release entry and goes on; with another template it refuses and runs nothing
